observed_response.note: The draft proposal is an authored scenario fixture for this fictional company, shown for comparison. It was not available to either candidate run. Overlap means the same clauses were touched; it says nothing about direction or merit.

review_notes: Reviewer note on S1: the candidate would shorten the remediation deadline for breaking changes published before July 20, 2027. That window is closed. Version 1.1 already shortened the forward-looking deadline to 15 calendar days, so this change restates a protection the current package contains and is not newly emerging drift. The original model wording is preserved.

Reviewer note on S2: the stated reason is that a two-Business-Day notice was missed, so the period should be shorter. A missed deadline does not show the deadline is too long; the September evidence points to a notice-routing failure. The one quotation that survived validation comes from the August incident, where notice was timely, and the September citation was dropped as unverifiable. The clause is reasonably identified as the place drift shows up; the proposed remedy is weakly supported.

What this run does show: with origination evidence alone the model keeps all eleven clauses; with the three detections it changes only the two operating covenants tied to the connector-reliability assumptions and retains the other nine. One run of each; stability is not measured.
